fix: Drop the snapshot Vec and iterate mutably. The fields `gestures` and `on_long_tap_down` are disjoint, so the borrow checker allows it: `for (pointer, gesture) in self.gestures.iter_mut() { if !gesture.long_tap.is_some_and(|deadline| deadline <= now) { continue; } gesture.long_tap = None; let details = TapDownDetails { global_position: gesture.last.0, local_position: gesture.last.1, kind: gesture.kind }; if let Some(callback) = &self.on_long_tap_down { callback(*pointer, details); } }`. The user callback cannot reach the recognizer, so no re-entrancy. Removes the per-poll collect.

Avoid the per-poll Vec. `start_drag` needs `&mut self` as a whole, so the snapshot exists to dodge a borrow error (§19). Find one due pointer at a time instead: `while let Some(pointer) = self.pointers.iter().find(|(_, state)| state.timer.is_some_and(|deadline| deadline <= now)).map(|(pointer, _)| *pointer) { let Some(state) = self.pointers.get_mut(&pointer) else { continue; }; state.timer = None; ...existing body... }`. The body clears `timer` first, so each iteration makes progress. The BTreeMap order is unchanged. The find is O(n) per fired timer, and n is tiny. Alternative: a reusable `due: Vec<u64>` field, cleared and refilled in `poll`.
